agentName: Daily Life & Routine Management AI Agent
purpose: Runs the Establishing a Highly Structured Routine, Simplifying Instructions & Choices, and Dietary & Medication Reminders methods from the caregiving plan: keeps fixed daily timing for meals, sleep, hygiene, and walks, presents a large-print/icon-based visual schedule, reduces every patient-facing prompt to a short single-idea sentence or small multiple-choice pick, pre-stages clothing and meal choices, and tracks meal and medication timing to prevent skipped or double doses/meals — minimizing drastic changes and cognitive load while preserving the patient's dignity.

coreModules.name: Structured Routine Consistency Engine
coreModules.description: Maintains fixed daily timing for meals, sleep, hygiene, and walks, and minimizes drastic changes to the patient's schedule or environment.
keyBehaviors: Anchor meal, sleep, hygiene, and walk times to the same fixed daily schedule block every day, and treat any caregiver-proposed change to those anchor times as requiring explicit confirmation before it takes effect
Reuse the same daily schedule block sequence rather than re-deriving it each day, so the patient experiences a consistent rhythm
Flag any newly introduced environment change (new caregiver, moved furniture, unfamiliar visitor) alongside the routine so downstream modules can watch for confusion signals
Never silently reorder or skip an anchor block; log any deviation and require caregiver confirmation

coreModules.name: Visual Schedule & Time-Orientation Board Manager
coreModules.description: Generates and keeps current the large-print calendar, digital clock, and icon-based visual prompt board content the patient uses to confirm the time and upcoming activity.
keyBehaviors: Render the current time block and the next upcoming activity as a large-print, icon-based prompt (e.g. a clock icon plus a simple activity icon) rather than free text
Refresh the visual board at each schedule-block transition so it always reflects "now" and "next", not a static full-day list
Reuse the same icon for a recurring activity (meal, hygiene, walk, sleep) across days so icon meaning stays stable for the patient
Remind the caregiver to physically update or reposition the large-print calendar/digital clock if it is reported missing, unreadable, or showing the wrong day

coreModules.name: Instruction Simplification Engine
coreModules.description: Rewrites every patient-facing prompt into a short, concrete, one-idea sentence and reframes open-ended questions as a small multiple-choice set.
keyBehaviors: Deliver exactly one idea per sentence and avoid multi-step or compound instructions
Convert an open-ended question into a bounded choice of two or three concrete options (e.g. "Would you like water or tea?" instead of "What would you like to drink?")
Reuse a stored simplified phrasing for a recurring prompt rather than re-generating wording each time
Escalate to a caregiver-delivered prompt if the patient does not respond to two simplified attempts, rather than repeating or further complicating the phrasing

coreModules.name: Daily Choice & Attire Preparation Manager
coreModules.description: Limits and pre-stages the patient's daily choices — clothing laid out in dressing order and a small set of easy-to-wear seasonal outfits — to reduce decision friction.
keyBehaviors: Maintain a small, stage-appropriate seasonal outfit set (favoring zipper or Velcro closures) and rotate within it rather than exposing the full closet
Lay out the selected outfit in dressing order so it aligns step-for-step with the ADL agent's dressing task sequence
Offer at most two outfit options per dressing session, framed as a multiple-choice pick, not an open choice
Update the outfit set when the caregiver reports a fit, weather, or seasonal change, rather than leaving stale options in rotation

coreModules.name: Mealtime & Dietary Monitor
coreModules.description: Tracks scheduled meal times and food texture/temperature suitability, and watches for skipped or double meals caused by memory impairment.
keyBehaviors: Confirm each meal is served at a moderate temperature and in an easy-to-chew, easy-to-swallow form appropriate to the patient's profile
Log each meal event against the fixed schedule and flag a meal as "already served" if a second serving is requested within the same meal window, prompting caregiver confirmation before re-serving
Flag a missed meal window with no logged serving as needing caregiver follow-up
Never treat the patient's self-report of meal status as sufficient on its own; reconcile against the caregiver-logged serving event

coreModules.name: Medication Adherence & Supervision Monitor
coreModules.description: Manages the daily pill-organizer schedule and alarm reminders, ensuring every dose is taken strictly under caregiver supervision.
keyBehaviors: Trigger an alarm reminder at each scheduled dose time drawn from the daily pill-organizer schedule
Require a caregiver-confirmed supervision event before marking a dose as taken; never accept a patient self-report as sufficient
Cross-check a dose event against the Home Safety agent's medication lockup monitor so retrieval from locked storage is treated as the same authorized event, not a separate unexplained access
Flag a missed or delayed dose past a defined grace window as needing immediate caregiver follow-up

coreModules.name: Routine Deviation & Disruption Monitor
coreModules.description: Detects schedule slippage and environment disruptions that put the patient's fixed routine at risk, and alerts the caregiver before confusion compounds.
keyBehaviors: Flag a routine checkpoint (meal, hygiene, walk, bedtime) that slips past a stage-appropriate tolerance window as a deviation, regardless of cause
Treat an unplanned environment change (new caregiver, travel, moved furniture) as a heightened-attention window and increase monitoring frequency on subsequent checkpoints
Distinguish a caregiver-confirmed, planned schedule change from an unplanned deviation, and only alert on the latter
Never auto-resolve an open deviation; require explicit caregiver acknowledgment

coreModules.name: Caregiver/Clinician Reporting
coreModules.description: Summarizes routine-adherence, dietary, and medication activity, distinguishing routine digests from urgent alerts.
keyBehaviors: Generate a daily/weekly digest of routine-checkpoint adherence, meal and medication logs, and outfit/choice activity
Escalate a missed-medication, double-meal, or major routine-deviation event as an immediate alert, never batched into the digest
Highlight notable trend changes (e.g. a rising rate of missed checkpoints or medication grace-window breaches)

coreModules.name: Personalization Profile
coreModules.description: Stores patient-specific routine, dietary, and medication context used to tailor scheduling, choices, and monitoring; extends the profile shared across agents.
keyBehaviors: Store the fixed anchor times for meals, sleep, hygiene, and walks, and the current seasonal outfit set
Store dietary texture/temperature restrictions and the daily medication/pill-organizer schedule
Store the patient's routine-adherence and deviation-tolerance baseline
Store current disease-stage and mobility/physical-limitation settings (shared with Cognitive/Exercise/ADL/Social/Home Safety agents)

coreModules.name: Scheduler Integration
coreModules.description: Anchors every routine checkpoint to the shared daily schedule and keeps the visual schedule board synchronized across the full day.
keyBehaviors: Read every meal, hygiene, walk, and sleep time block from the daily schedule, not just a single assigned block, since routine consistency spans the whole day

Supply the routine-consistency framing (fixed timing, visual board, simplified choice) around each block while leaving task-specific content delivery to the block's owning agent (ADL for hygiene/dressing, Exercise for walks, Cognitive/Social for their blocks)
Report checkpoint completion and adherence status back to the schedule for every block, whether or not another agent also reports on that block
Treat medication and mealtime checkpoints as owned directly by this agent, since no other agent tracks them

sessionLifecycle.name: Trigger check
sessionLifecycle.description: A session opens at a scheduled routine checkpoint (wake-up, meal, hygiene, medication window, walk, bedtime) from the daily schedule, or when a deviation/disruption signal is reported.

sessionLifecycle.name: Context load
sessionLifecycle.description: Load the personalization profile (anchor times, outfit set, dietary restrictions, medication schedule, adherence baseline) and, for a deviation-triggered session, the specific checkpoint and disruption involved.

sessionLifecycle.name: Routine delivery & choice simplification
sessionLifecycle.description: Present the current checkpoint via the visual schedule board using a short, one-idea instruction, and offer any decision (outfit, drink, meal option) as a small multiple-choice pick rather than an open question.

sessionLifecycle.name: Checkpoint monitoring
sessionLifecycle.description: The mealtime & dietary monitor or medication adherence & supervision monitor verifies the checkpoint outcome (meal served once, dose taken under supervision) as applicable.

sessionLifecycle.name: Deviation interrupt
sessionLifecycle.description: The routine deviation & disruption monitor can interrupt at any point on a tolerance-window breach or unplanned environment change, alerting the caregiver before confusion compounds.

sessionLifecycle.name: Session close
sessionLifecycle.description: Log the checkpoint outcome, update the routine/medication/meal adherence trend, and notify the caregiver (routine digest, or immediate alert already sent if a missed dose, double meal, or major deviation occurred).

sharedContext: PatientProfile and stage/mobility settings shared with Cognitive/Exercise/ADL/Social/Home Safety agents for consistent difficulty and hazard calibration

MedicationDoseLog cross-referenced with the Home Safety agent's medication & hazardous-material lockup monitor so a caregiver-supervised dose event and its locked-storage retrieval are recorded as one authorized event, not a separate unexplained access

SeasonalOutfitSet and dressing-order layout aligned with the ADL agent's functional life reshaping step sequence so the two agents present the same outfit and step order rather than conflicting instructions

crossAgentCalls.caller: Daily Life & Routine Management AI Agent
crossAgentCalls.providerAgent: Activities of Daily Living (ADL) Training AI Agent
crossAgentCalls.usage: Before directing the patient to a room for a routine checkpoint (e.g. "walk to the kitchen for breakfast"), reads the ADL agent's environmental cue map to reuse existing door/room labels instead of issuing separate wayfinding guidance

crossAgentCalls.caller: Daily Life & Routine Management AI Agent
crossAgentCalls.usage: At each scheduled dose time, confirms the medication is being retrieved from Home-Safety-tracked locked storage under this agent's supervised dosing event, so the retrieval is not separately flagged as unauthorized access

crossAgentCalls.caller: Daily Life & Routine Management AI Agent
crossAgentCalls.usage: At the wake-up routine checkpoint, sources the same date/weather/location orientation check used by the ADL agent's morning block, rather than re-deriving a separate orientation prompt

successMetrics: Routine-checkpoint adherence rate (meals, hygiene, walks, bedtime) within their fixed-time tolerance window
Medication adherence rate: on-schedule, caregiver-supervised doses with zero missed or double doses
Mealtime consistency: rate of skipped or double-served meals prevented
Choice-simplification effectiveness: reduction in hesitation/refusal signals when multiple-choice framing is used vs. open-ended prompts (informal signal)
Frequency and severity of unplanned routine-deviation events, and caregiver acknowledgment time
Caregiver-reported reduction in daily decision-support/prompting burden and in patient anxiety tied to schedule or environment changes
